## The problem

Control closes the loop: the controller must keep the system within its requirements. Here,
resilience is understood broadly: controlling very complex systems with today's performance
criteria, such as frugality; planning the paths of teams of robots or drones; keeping the
system in operational condition when faults occur, which calls for maintenance, repair and the
reconfiguration of its control; and withstanding cyber-attacks on actuators and sensors.
Supervisory Control Theory provides controllers that are correct by construction, but its
classical setting assumes a single, reliable model. My work extends it, with the help of the
digital twin, to systems that are concurrent, switch between modes, are reconfigured or are
attacked, and to high-level tasks expressed in temporal logics.

## Contributions

- **Concurrent controllers for complex systems.** Higher-dimensional automata, a model of
  non-interleaving concurrency, to turn controllers specified as interpreted Petri nets into
  closed-loop controllers and reveal ambiguous or contradictory specifications.
- **Multi-robot path planning with temporal logics.** Counting Time Temporal Logic, which
  counts how many times a sub-task is satisfied, solved by integer linear programming and
  tested on mobile robots, with Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Xiang Yin) and the University of
  Zaragoza (Cristian Mahulea); path planning for drones is explored in MSc internships with
  Osaka Metropolitan University (Kai Cai). The same logics plan the daily activities of older
  people at home according to medical recommendations.
- **Reconfiguration and safe mode switching.** Each operating mode is designed separately,
  then the conflicts between modes are resolved to obtain ready-to-use control laws, with the
  conditions under which this multi-model approach behaves like the centralized one; control
  laws are reconfigured when the system changes, for instance after a fault.
- **Resilience to cyber-attacks.** Supervisors that withstand a prescribed number of attacks
  on actuators and on sensors, with Osaka Metropolitan University (Kai Cai); reconfiguration of
  the control of a cyber-physical system under attack, using its digital twin.

## Selected publications

- [Supervisory Control Under Indefinite Actuator and Sensor Attacks: Prescribed Resilience](https://doi.org/10.1109/tac.2026.3665131) — *IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control*, 2026. [Industrial & critical systems]{.domain-tag .domain-industry}\
  [Designs supervisors with a prescribed resilience: each unsafe state is protected against a given number of attacks on actuators and on sensors.]{.contribution}
- [Automatic Activity Planning Based on Activity Daily Living and Quality of Life Recommendations](https://doi.org/10.1109/wodes69290.2026.11598225) — *WODES*, 2026. [Human & health]{.domain-tag .domain-human}\
  [Combines probabilistic models of a person's daily activities with medical recommendations to propose a personalized activity program, using variants of linear temporal logic.]{.contribution}
- [Interpreted Higher-Dimensional Automata for Concurrent Discrete-Event Control](https://doi.org/10.1109/wodes69290.2026.11598183) — *WODES*, 2026. [Industrial & critical systems]{.domain-tag .domain-industry}\
  [Uses higher-dimensional automata to turn controllers given as interpreted Petri nets into closed-loop controllers, revealing ambiguous or contradictory specifications.]{.contribution}
- [Counting Time Temporal Logic for Multi-Robot Path Planning in Finite Horizons](https://doi.org/10.1109/tase.2025.3636053) — *IEEE T-ASE*, 2025.\
  [Extends linear temporal logic to count how many times a sub-task is satisfied, and solves the resulting multi-robot path planning problem by integer linear programming.]{.contribution}
- [Equivalence of behaviors between centralized and multi-model approaches](https://hal.science/hal-00759500) — *IEEE CASE*, 2011. [Industrial & critical systems]{.domain-tag .domain-industry}\
  [Gives the conditions under which the multi-model approach, with smaller models, yields the same controlled behavior as the centralized one.]{.contribution}
- [Formal Approach to Multimodal Control Design: Application to Mode Switching](https://hal.science/hal-00471885) — *IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics*, 2009. [Industrial & critical systems]{.domain-tag .domain-industry}\
  [A supervisory-control framework to design each operating mode separately, then resolve the conflicts between modes to obtain ready-to-use control laws.]{.contribution}
